claim: The 442nd took more casualties than the number of men it rescued.
source: [1] 442nd Regimental Combat Team, rescue of the Lost Battalion (1st Battalion, 141st Infantry Regiment), Vosges Mountains, October 24–30, 1944. Unit citations and casualty records, U.S. Army Center of Military History. The "most decorated for its size and length of service" characterization is the Army's own.

claim: He was therefore free to be exactly what he was, and what he was is documented: the Munson and Ringle reports, prepared for the American government before internment, both found the population overwhelmingly loyal and internment unnecessary.
source: [2a] The Munson Report (Curtis B. Munson, prepared for the State Department and delivered to the President in November 1941) and the Ringle Report (Lt. Cmdr. Kenneth Ringle, Office of Naval Intelligence, January 1942) both concluded that the Japanese American population was overwhelmingly loyal and that mass internment was unnecessary. Both preceded Executive Order 9066. The Commission on Wartime Relocation and Internment of Civilians reached the same conclusion in *Personal Justice Denied* (1983), finding that military necessity had not justified the exclusion.

claim: Sun Yat-sen, honored on both sides of the strait as the founder of the Chinese republic, spent his formative years in Hawaii, sent as a boy to live with his elder brother in Honolulu, where he attended Iolani School and then Oahu College, the school known today as Punahou, which would a century later educate a future American president.
source: [2] Sun Yat-sen attended Iolani School (1879–1882) and Oahu College, now Punahou School (1882–1883). His articulation of the Three Principles of the People and its acknowledged debt to Lincoln's Gettysburg formulation are documented in his own writings and lectures.

claim: Its rule produced the deadliest famine in recorded history, tens of millions dead in the Great Leap Forward from policies the Party itself imposed, followed by the Cultural Revolution it unleashed upon its own people.
source: [3] Great Leap Forward mortality estimates range widely across scholarly sources, from roughly fifteen million to forty-five million. The text says "tens of millions," which every major estimate supports, and avoids a point figure no source establishes definitively.

claim: The 2017 National Intelligence Law states, in Article 7, that any organization or citizen must support, assist, and cooperate with state intelligence work.
source: [4] National Security Law of the People's Republic of China (2015), Article 11; National Intelligence Law of the People's Republic of China (2017), Article 7. These are the adversary's own published statutes and require no interpretation to establish the compulsion. Everything else in this chapter is secondary to them.

section: Economic: Dual-Use and the Hardware in the Walls
claim: Department of Defense's list of Chinese military companies won American transit contracts on price alone, placing its cars beneath major cities through ordinary procurement that triggered no national-security review.
source: [5] Department of Defense designations of Chinese military companies (Section 1260H list) and Department of Commerce Entity List determinations, both published in the Federal Register. The rail-car case concerns a subsidiary of a designated parent winning U.S. transit procurement; the procurement itself triggered no national-security review, which is the point the example is making.

claim: Talent-recruitment programs, led by the Thousand Talents Plan, draw established researchers toward Chinese institutions with funding and prestige, while the United Front Work Department cultivates the overseas Chinese community, professional associations, and friendly foreign elites.
source: [6] Thousand Talents Plan documented in Chinese government program materials and in U.S. congressional testimony, including Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations work on foreign talent recruitment. Individual prosecutions arising from undisclosed foreign funding are matters of court record.
